questions.stem: A quick scenario: Noah Rivera wants $7,500 in 2 years. At an annual return of 10%, how much must be invested today to reach that goal?

questions.learningObjective: Apply bonds and interest rates concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: A practical case: Owen Haddad invests $4,500 at 8% interest compounded annually for 2 years. What is the balance at the end?

options.misconception: uses one fewer compounding period than stated
reports interest earned rather than the ending balance
uses simple interest instead of annual compounding

questions.explanation: Compounding applies the growth rate to the previous balance each year, so the balance is principal times one plus the rate raised to the number of years. That gives $5,248.8 after 2 years. Simple interest, interest alone, or the wrong period count each misses part of the effect.
questions.hint: Compound growth uses an exponent equal to the number of years.

questions.subject: PERSONAL_FINANCE
questions.learningObjective: Apply bonds and interest rates concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: Consider this: Hana Kowalski deposits $3,000 in an account paying 3% simple interest for 4 years. How much interest is earned over the full term?

options.misconception: treats the percentage as a whole-number multiplier
adds the principal, giving the balance rather than the interest
counts only one year of interest instead of the whole term

questions.explanation: Simple interest equals principal times rate times time, with the rate written as a decimal. Here that is $3,000 times 3% times 4 years, which gives $360. One year of interest or the ending balance would answer a different question.
questions.hint: Use I = P times r times t, with r as a decimal.
